# PAA Authority Stack And Operator Architecture

## Vision Marker

This document is a Vision-layer authority document.

It defines the system-level frame that later Design, Plan, and Build artifacts must follow.

## Core Statement

PAA is not only a planning toolkit.
PAA is the authority operating system for authority-driven software development.

The PAA system must be able to:
- define and govern its own authority
- bootstrap itself through its own methodology
- consume downstream project authority such as Baby-7 / Fractal Core
- derive executable work from that authority
- coordinate runtime workers and agent-host programs that implement, verify, and accept slices
- expose a real operator surface for human control and inspection

## Strategic Context

Two major authority layers already exist and must remain explicit.

### Layer A: Source / domain authority
This is the durable, project-specific truth captured from Tom's ideas, corrections, constraints, examples, and code-derived findings.

Primary sources include:
- `/Users/billyweisberg/Repos/Individual-Centricity/appdev/docs/architecture/tom-baby7-fractal-core/`
- `/Users/billyweisberg/Repos/Individual-Centricity/appdev-arch/docs/architecture/tom-baby7-fractal-core/project-authority/`

This layer already contains:
- architecture docs
- normative behavior definitions
- parity and tolerance rules
- CLI host expectations
- handoff workflow and queue rules
- task-authority workflows
- issue materialization rules
- project authority schemas
- handoff packet schemas
- artifact schemas

### Layer B: PAA operational authority
This is the structured authority that PAA creates and manages in order to operationalize source authority.

Examples include:
- component specs
- implementation plans
- activities and dependencies
- realization states
- derivation-readiness truth
- runtime service decomposition truth

### Layer C: Runtime execution state
This is the live operational state of the automated system.

Examples include:
- queue messages and claim state
- packet histories
- worker execution state
- verification results
- issue and PR transitions
- runtime diagnostics
- delivery and closeout evidence

The runtime execution tier is agent-oriented.

Meaning:
- PAA remains the authority and orchestration system
- worker-host programs invoke LLM-based agents only inside bounded, deterministic run envelopes
- agent state must not replace published authority, queue truth, or structured verification state

## Core Architectural Principle

PAA must preserve all three layers instead of collapsing them.

### Source authority is not replaced
The source authority remains the durable statement of what the project is and what it must preserve.

### PAA operational authority is not informal glue
The operational layer is the structured derivation and governance substrate that lets authority become executable.

### Runtime state is not planning truth
The runtime layer records live execution and orchestration state. It must not become the substitute for published authority.

## Bootstrap Principle

PAA must be self-reflective.

Meaning:
- PAA should use its own authority patterns to build and refine itself
- the PAA authority set is the first serious proving example of the methodology
- the system must be able to operate its own component realization, planning, and worker automation lanes
- once stable, the same machinery should be able to operate downstream authority such as Baby-7 / Fractal Core

This is bootstrapping, not duplication.

## Authority Stack

### Tier 1: Source authority tier
Owns:
- domain architecture
- behavioral requirements
- queue workflow rules
- proving and parity requirements
- task-authority publication
- machine-readable project authority and packet schemas

### Tier 2: PAA operational authority tier
Owns:
- normalization of authority into PAA structures
- component decomposition
- implementation plan truth
- activity progress and completion state
- successor slice derivation
- operator-facing planning truth

### Tier 3: Runtime orchestration tier
Owns:
- worker execution
- agent-host execution envelopes
- queue consumption and handoff
- packet transport and validation
- verification execution
- acceptance transitions
- diagnostics and reporting

## Operator Architecture

The operator architecture must expose the full authority stack as one coherent system.

It must allow an operator to:
- inspect source authority
- validate structured authority
- derive executable state
- start and monitor workers
- inspect queue flow
- run verification
- accept or reject slices
- inspect progress and reports

It must also allow an operator to:
- inspect worker-host context assembly
- inspect bounded agent invocation inputs
- inspect normalized agent results before or after packet publication

The operator surface must not require thread memory or implicit knowledge of repository history.

## System Zones

### Producer zone
Purpose:
- manage authority and derivation

Owns:
- authority inspection
- structured materialization
- plan derivation
- progress reconciliation
- next-slice derivation
- reporting from operational authority

### Consumer zone
Purpose:
- manage runtime workers and execution orchestration

Owns:
- worker services
- bounded agent-host programs
- queue operations
- runtime dispatch
- packet handling
- verification runtime operations
- acceptance-time transitions

### Core zone
Purpose:
- hold the shared deterministic model and decision substrate

Owns:
- repositories
- service contracts
- DTOs
- decision services
- validation logic
- implementation-plan progress logic
- lifecycle services
- shared packet models

## Relationship To Baby-7 / Fractal Core

Baby-7 / Fractal Core is the first major downstream authority family that should be run through the PAA system.

This means the final PAA operator system must be able to:
- read and validate the published Fractal Core authority manifest
- validate task slices against project authority schemas
- materialize issues and briefs from that authority
- orchestrate TechLead / Dev / QA runtime workers using the published packet schemas
- execute Dev and QA work through bounded Microsoft Agent Framework worker-host programs when those roles require model-driven reasoning
- verify parity, tolerances, and protected-path expectations where required

The goal is not to duplicate the Baby-7 authority docs inside PAA.
The goal is to make PAA the system that can operate them.

## Near-Term Objective

The next design and build work should create:
1. a full PAA CLI architecture
2. a PAA worker runtime architecture
3. an implementation plan for building the operator system

These must be derived from this authority-stack framing rather than designed in isolation.

## Constraints

The operator system must:
- remain authority-first
- remain deterministic at the authority, packet, and acceptance layers
- fail closed when required authority is missing
- preserve the separation between published authority and runtime state
- avoid duplicate control planes
- support self-bootstrap first, then downstream authority operation

Agent execution must be used:
- at the right time
- for the right bounded responsibilities
- inside explicit worker-host programs
- with normalized outputs that return to PAA packet and model truth

## Non-Goals

This document does not define:
- detailed command syntax
- worker implementation classes
- queue transport internals
- concrete DB schema changes
- UI/dashboard design

Those belong in downstream Design and Plan artifacts.
